title.en: SMT arithmetic: integer and real models

summary: Compare exact arithmetic domains and preserve solver uncertainty in the display.
objective: Build a constraint inspector where I switch x between Int and Real for 2x=1, inspect a returned model and distinguish SAT, UNSAT and unknown.
intent_signals: Build a constraint inspector where I switch x between Int and Real for 2x=1, inspect a returned model and distinguish SAT, UNSAT and unknown.
example_prompts: Build a constraint inspector where I switch x between Int and Real for 2x=1, inspect a returned model and distinguish SAT, UNSAT and unknown.
negative_signals: No nonlinear/quantified arithmetic, floating-point theory, optimizer, automatic solver installation or guarantee of a decisive response within a resource limit.
not_for: No nonlinear/quantified arithmetic, floating-point theory, optimizer, automatic solver installation or guarantee of a decisive response within a resource limit.

entities.name: Constraint region
entities.guidance: For two variables use a labeled XY slice; a third declared numeric variable can own Z. Show integer lattice points distinctly from continuous real regions and retain exact rational labels.

entities.name: Solver result card
entities.guidance: Keep model values next to the exact submitted formula. Unknown has no green feasible-region badge, and a missing backend is unavailable rather than UNSAT.

state_contract.model: Quantifier-free linear arithmetic with up to three declared variables, rational constants and Bool combinations of equalities/inequalities. Use a real SMT backend or provenance-labeled imported results bound to a formula hash. Track not-run/running/sat/unsat/unknown/error distinctly, plus exact model values and backend reason. A viewport window does not bound the logical domain.
state_contract.authority: The typed domain model owns each committed state and result. Geometry, labels and selection derive from that model; animation cannot certify a claim.
actions: Edit constraints or sorts and clear old results.
Run an available backend or load a labeled result; select an assertion and inspect model evaluation.
Compare 2x=1 over Int versus Real; inspect actual unknown responses and their supplied reason.

invariants: Re-evaluate a SAT witness against every submitted assertion using exact supported arithmetic; never treat approximate shading as a witness.
Expected arithmetic example: integer case UNSAT, real case SAT with x=1/2.
Unknown does not resolve satisfiability. An unsat core is a selected conflicting subset, not automatically a minimal subset or independently checked proof.
motion_guidance: Step commits one semantic action; pause freezes presentation and leaves the committed state inspectable. Reset cancels pending playback and restores the complete starting state.
Offer a static transition highlight and an equivalent readable table for reduced motion. Camera travel is presentation, not an inference or domain operation.
creative_affordances: Use shallow sculptural cards, restrained materials and selective focus to expose relationships. Prefer a flat readable layout whenever depth has no declared role.
known_limits: No nonlinear/quantified arithmetic, floating-point theory, optimizer, automatic solver installation or guarantee of a decisive response within a resource limit.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no generated artifact, solver integration, runtime behavior or visual check has run.

physical_contract.scope: Abstract symbols and logical state; mesh contact, light and motion have no causal role in the model.

object_craft.structure: For two variables use a labeled XY slice; a third declared numeric variable can own Z. Show integer lattice points distinctly from continuous real regions and retain exact rational labels.
object_craft.material: Matte surfaces and high-contrast labels; distinguish status with text and border style as well as color.

claims.statement: SMT formulas use declared sorts, including unbounded integers and reals; arithmetic satisfiability and extracted models respect those sorts.
claims.scope: Quantifier-free linear arithmetic subset; exact integers/rationals, not machine floating point.

claims.statement: Z3 exposes a separate unknown result and its explanation; retrieving a proof requires the appropriate proof-enabled UNSAT result, and unsat cores are not minimized by default.
claims.scope: Official solver-result API contract, not a guarantee that every query produces a proof or model.
